document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Coordinating Our Efforts and Sharpening Our Message on Bin Ladin
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Secret] Recommends working closely with the Saudis, the cornerstone of U.S. efforts, and sharpening the message to Pakistan and the Taliban on expelling bin Laden. It suggests Saudi pressure on Taliban trade via the UAE, says Pakistan's lack of support must change, and notes Mullah Omar appears strongly committed to bin Laden. Excised.

events.description: US Embassy Islamabad cable recommending coordination with Saudi Arabia and sharper messaging to Pakistan and Taliban on Bin Ladin.
Brahimi met the US Ambassador and explained support for the Tashkent meeting.
Prince Turki flown to Kandahar by Pakistan to intervene with the Taliban over Bin Ladin.
Taliban killing of hundreds if not thousands of Shi'a and other non-combatants at Mazar-i-Sharif.
US strikes on Khost, described as a wasting asset.
US Embassy Islamabad cable recommending coordination with Saudi Arabia and sharpened messaging to Pakistan and Taliban on Bin Ladin.
Brahimi met the US Ambassador and explained his support for a Tashkent Six-Plus-Two meeting.
Taliban killed hundreds or thousands of Shi'a and non-combatants at Mazar-i-Sharif.
Pakistan flew Saudi intelligence chief Prince Turki to Kandahar to intervene with the Taliban on Bin Ladin.
US strikes on Khost referenced as a 'wasting asset'.
Saudi Arabia decided to downgrade ties with the Taliban.
Karimov and Yeltsin discussions in Tashkent; agreed to invite all factions.
Killings of several UN employees earlier in the year in Afghanistan.

U.S. Embassy Islamabad sent cable section 3 of 3 on coordinating efforts on Bin Ladin. It critiques the proposed 'Six-Plus-Two plus factions' meeting in Tashkent and suggests a Six-Plus-Two meeting in New York to review the Tashkent meeting's structure and agenda.

Proposed Tashkent meeting of all Afghan factions with Six-Plus-Two states, supported by Brahimi; the embassy warns it could raise regional tensions and suggests a Six-Plus-Two meeting in New York first.

key_claims: The Embassy judged Bin Ladin's continued presence in Afghanistan the most important Afghan policy issue.
Mullah Omar appears strongly committed to Bin Ladin and may not be influenced by US or Saudi pressure.
Pakistan has the closest Taliban ties but had done little beyond flying Prince Turki to Kandahar.
The Taliban might hand Bin Ladin to Saudi Arabia but not to the US.
The UAE is the Taliban's major trade and smuggling entrepot.
US press claims crediting Turki's intervention were seen as unhelpful.
The Embassy advised moving before the Khost strikes' deterrent effect faded.
